guide.title: Bethel, Connecticut: Barnum's Birthplace and a Vodka First
guide.intro: Bethel began as a parish of Danbury, taking its name in 1759 from the Hebrew for "House of God," and it did not become an independent Connecticut town until 1855. As part of Danbury, Bethel had hat-making factories as early as the late 1700s, and the trade stayed vital to the local economy well into the early 1900s. The town's best-known native is showman P.T. Barnum, born here on July 5, 1810; a downtown square still carries his name. Early-20th-century political cartoonist Art Young also lived much of his life in Bethel. In 1934 Rudolph Kunett is said to have opened the first vodka distillery in the United States here, after buying the rights to the Smirnoff recipe from the exiled Smirnoff family. Through the end of 2026, the town is running Bethel 250, a commemoration of the Declaration of Independence's 250th anniversary.

sections.heading: A hat town, a showman and a vodka first
sections.body: Hat manufacturing carried Bethel's economy for more than a century, a trade the town inherited from neighboring Danbury's factories as early as the late 1700s. P.T. Barnum, born in Bethel on July 5, 1810, went on to build a career as a showman and entrepreneur; P.T. Barnum Square in the village center still bears his name. Political cartoonist Art Young, one of the more controversial cartoonists of the early 20th century, lived much of his life here. In 1934, Rudolph Kunett is said to have opened the first vodka distillery in the United States in Bethel after acquiring U.S. rights to the recipe from the exiled Smirnoff family — a claim resting on a single account but consistent with the town's own telling of its history.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: Bethel sits in northern Fairfield County just southeast of Danbury, and Interstate 84 passes through town (Exit 8, Newtown Road). Bethel is also one of the few small Connecticut towns with its own commuter rail stop: Bethel station, 13 Durant Avenue, on Metro-North's Danbury Branch, with about 197 parking spaces and two EV chargers. Many weekday Danbury Branch trains continue straight through to Stamford and New York City without a change at South Norwalk, though off-peak trips generally do require that transfer. The branch is not electrified, so these are diesel-hauled trains. Ticket machines are not reported at the station — buy tickets in advance through the TrainTime app. HART Route 5 connects at Bethel station. No Amtrak, Shore Line East, or CTrail Hartford Line service reaches Bethel.

sections.heading: Two neighboring state parks and a downtown of pizzerias
sections.body: Two state parks reach into Bethel from next door in Redding. Putnam Memorial State Park, the Continental Army's 1778-79 winter encampment site known as "Connecticut's Valley Forge," sits just over the line in Redding. Collis P. Huntington State Park, 1,017 acres of ponds, a lagoon and about ten miles of trails guarded at the entrance by Anna Hyatt Huntington's bronze bears and wolves, is centered in Redding but its grounds spread into Bethel and Newtown too. Downtown, Greenwood Avenue carries Bethel's restaurant scene: Bethel Pizza House and Village Pizzeria near the I-84 approach both keep loyal followings, Grassy Plain Pizzeria serves the Grassy Plain Street side of town, and Portofino Restaurant & Wine Bar is the sit-down option for a slower dinner. Jubi Tea & Sweets pours bubble tea and matcha in the heart of downtown.

faq.question: How do I get to Bethel?
faq.answer: By car — I-84 passes through Bethel at Exit 8 (Newtown Road). Bethel also has its own Metro-North Danbury Branch station at 13 Durant Avenue; many weekday trains run through to Stamford and New York City without a change at South Norwalk, though off-peak trips typically require one.

faq.question: Is there a train to Bethel?
faq.answer: Yes — Bethel station, 13 Durant Avenue, is a stop on Metro-North's Danbury Branch. The branch is not electrified, so trains are diesel-hauled, and there are no ticket machines at the station; buy in advance through the TrainTime app.

faq.question: Is Collis P. Huntington State Park in Bethel?
faq.answer: The park's grounds reach into Bethel, but its official address and the bulk of its 1,017 acres are in neighboring Redding, along with a corner in Newtown. Bronze bear and wolf sculptures by Anna Hyatt Huntington stand at the entrance. Open daily 8 a.m. to sunset, free admission, leashed pets allowed.

faq.question: Is there a hotel in Bethel?
faq.answer: No lodging inside Bethel could be verified. The nearest confirmed option is the Ethan Allen Hotel in neighboring Danbury, about five miles away.

faq.question: Where is Putnam Memorial State Park?
faq.answer: In neighboring Redding, not Bethel — the Continental Army's 1778-79 winter encampment site, sometimes called "Connecticut's Valley Forge."

places.name: Bethel Public Library
places.summary: The town's public library anchors the Greenwood Avenue downtown with an active calendar for adults, teens and children, including programming tied to the Bethel 250 anniversary commemoration. Phone (203) 794-8756.

places.name: Bethel Land Trust Preserves
places.address: Bethel, CT 06801 (multiple trailheads; check the land trust's site before visiting)
places.summary: A network of small, free, publicly accessible preserves around town, including the 4.7-acre Wolfpit Preserve, the 10-acre Janet P. Miller Preserve, Skyedge Preserve, Mike's Pond and Ivy Island, linked in part by the Boardwalk on the Enchanted Trail. Street addresses and trailheads are not published on the land trust's site — check before visiting.

places.name: Jubi Tea & Sweets
places.summary: Downtown bubble tea and dessert shop serving handcrafted boba, premium matcha, fruit teas, bubble waffles and rotating gluten-free macarons. Open Mon-Sat noon-8:30 p.m., Sun noon-6 p.m. Phone (203) 616-5368.

places.name: Bethel Pizza House
places.summary: Long-running Greenwood Avenue pizzeria with classic and specialty pies, gluten-free crust on most, calzones, grinders and baked pastas. Phone (203) 748-1427.

places.name: Grassy Plain Pizzeria & Restaurant
places.summary: Neighborhood pizzeria and sit-down restaurant on the Grassy Plain Street side of town, away from the Greenwood Avenue strip. Phone (203) 743-6600.

places.name: Village Pizzeria
places.summary: Pizzeria on the Stony Hill Road corridor near the I-84 approach — convenient for travelers coming off the highway. Phone (203) 780-0337.

places.name: Portofino Restaurant & Wine Bar
places.summary: Italian restaurant and wine bar in the downtown Greenwood Avenue block, the most sit-down, evening-oriented of Bethel's independent restaurants. Evening hours are not published — call ahead. Phone (203) 797-8131.

Bethel borders Redding; Putnam Memorial State Park, "Connecticut's Valley Forge," sits just over the line in Redding.
Collis P. Huntington State Park is centered in Redding, but its grounds reach into Bethel and Newtown.
